# Owner-supplied Work artifacts — provenance and binding

Everything under this directory is a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy of files delivered by
the owner in the P4 data-instantiation readiness package
`P4_DATA_INSTANTIATION_READINESS_PACKAGE_2026-09-13.zip`
(SHA-256 `6d8473ce074ee34ea0ee117b596a595b2844d8cd8d05a4d16a4d79937d4eb1d2`,
verified against the owner's expected hash before unpacking; the package's
own `SHA256SUMS.txt` verified for every listed file). The copies are evidence
and proposed bindings from the owner's side; nothing here is generated by,
or derived from, the Go code under test, and nothing here is a production
fact, a dataset window, a frozen entropy schedule or a ruleset choice.

## What each file pins

- **Entropy vectors** (`entropy_python_vectors.json`,
  `entropy_node_vectors_and_controls.json`, `ENTROPY_CROSSCHECK.json`): two
  independent implementations (Python standard library; Node `crypto`) of the
  approved `p4-hmac-sha256-u64/v1` algorithm — public seed
  `SHA-256("BUKEROV|P4|COMMON_CUTOFF|v1")` =
  `c4c7808033ef29c21e7904c323b3554ae1bdf3aae69251972d0e7a72a80f59ca`, nine
  length-prefixed UTF-8 parts, HMAC-SHA256 under the raw seed, first eight
  bytes big-endian as sixteen lower-case hex digits — on seven synthetic
  vector points over two dataset/opportunity identities, cross-checked PASS.
  `entropy_work_test.go` requires the Go implementation to reproduce every
  message byte, byte length, message SHA-256, full HMAC and word exactly, and
  the Node negative controls (UTF-8 byte length, big-endian first eight,
  fixed-width zero).
- **Ruleset candidates** (`rulesets/`): two candidate P3b configurations in
  the raw-percentage basis, with raw-byte SHA-256 and an INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED
  native `pe-ors-config/v1` digest; the owner recorded the native Go digest as
  NOT_RUN and the owner binding as PENDING. `ruleset_work_test.go` runs the
  native digest and seam-6 verification on both. It chooses, ranks, tunes and
  compares nothing; the binding stays PENDING.

## Reproduction

The Go tests read these files and never write them. The owner's own
reproduction scripts (`synthetic/entropy_python.py`,
`synthetic/entropy_node/reproduce_entropy.mjs`,
`rulesets/build_validate_rulesets.py`) live in the package, not here.
